scope: ONLY exact standalone nofork identity and assertion-failure commands; no production lifecycle re-review

findings.title: Evidence-write failure after an unknown cleanup escapes the only owner
findings.trigger: The C remains live and cleanup returns unknown (for example fresh /proc EIO, an undeliverable signal, or no close). Writing outcome.json then throws ENOSPC/EIO/EACCES, or main's held.json write throws. Both happen after spawn and outside the owned try/finally/exception boundary.
findings.impact: runPilot/main rejects into unhandled top-level await. The detached nofork C can remain waiting forever for authorization with its owner gone. This is an ordinary evidence-I/O failure path, not an excluded external kill/OOM and not a production-N issue.
findings.contract: R4 SPEC unknown must retain the actual child/closePromise/root and must not top-level throw/exit losing C; original and cleanup failures retained.
findings.minimal_fix: In the two new files only, make the post-spawn owner survive every evidence/logging failure through terminal proof; retain primary plus evidence errors in memory and use a nonthrowing reporting path. The CLI must enter the same persistent owned unknown state before any exception can escape, and may return nonzero only after actual terminal proof. Do not add a responsibility timeout or delete the root.
findings.actual_branch_counterfactual: Import and invoke actual main/runPilot with injected deps and a fake child kept live; make writeEvidence throw only for outcome.json, then held.json. Assert no rejected top-level owner, the same child/closePromise/root remain retained and no premature terminal return; later actual fake exit+close+gone completes a failed result. Current tests invoke runPilot with writes that never fail and do not import main.
findings.runtime: NOT_RUN; static counterfactual, not a captured execution

findings.title: Recorded diagnostic and channel failures do not disqualify either mode
findings.trigger: A valid HELLO is received, but stdout/stderr exceeds64KiB or emits an error, or a malformed/oversize/error control event is recorded before final result. Ledger sets diagnosticsLost/stream errors/controlError, yet runPilot never uses those facts as a failure latch. identity kind depends only on primary, while assertion-failure passing checks only deliberate error+cleanup closed+epoch gone.
findings.impact: The exact CLI can report identity ok/exit0 or fault_case_passed=true despite a known required budget/transport failure. A decoder partial-buffer bound exists, but decoded frames can also accumulate without a frame/byte cap. Fixed reviewed noauthorize C has a small normal transcript, so this is not claimed as an observed or arbitrary external flood; the actual error-entry/result route nevertheless contradicts the required failure handling.
findings.contract: R4 SPEC stdout/control bounded and overflow/error fails while cleanup continues; deliberate assertion passes only its intended full verified case, not a different recorded failure.
findings.minimal_fix: Add one bounded first-failure latch wired from actual ledger event handlers and checked during HELLO, cleanup and final eligibility; preserve the intended primary plus cleanup/transport errors. Bound decoded queue/error storage without dropping needed first HELLO. Identity success must explicitly require proved closed+exit+original epoch gone and no disqualifying failure; expected assertion must be the sole intended primary with all required facts.
findings.actual_branch_counterfactual: Through actual runPilot/main, deliver legal HELLO followed by each stdout overflow, stderr error, invalid control data and socket error, including in the same turn as TERM/close. Assert safe cleanup still completes, but neither identity ok nor fault_case_passed can be emitted. Test decoded many-frame arrivals for a real bounded queue. Existing stream-error/budget tests only inspect ledger fields.

findings.title: HELD branch treats a close promise alone as the final terminal proof
findings.trigger: cleanup is unknown because fresh original-epoch presence is unknown (or a close was seen while its epoch still appears present). main awaits the shared closePromise and immediately writes closed-after-held/returns1. If close was already seen, this await resolves immediately; there is no new exit/no-birth consistency or fresh epoch-gone check.
findings.impact: A deadline initially returns honest unknown, but the CLI later retires that unknown without proving the specified complete terminal facts. main never re-finalizes the tagged cleanup or checks exitSeen. This finding does not assert that ordinary Node close is a stream-only event or that a live normal child naturally emits close: Node close usually follows exit, but the task explicitly requires independent fresh epoch confirmation and truthful continued ownership on uncertainty.
findings.contract: R4 SPEC true close plus exit/no-birth and fresh original epoch gone before completion; receipt EOF/error/timeout is not process end; unknown keeps the owner until proved.
findings.minimal_fix: Continue the same owner state machine after close until exit/no-birth facts and fresh epoch-gone are all confirmed, using bounded referenced polling and nonthrowing evidence handling. Reuse the persistent close ledger; do not signal an exited/reaped child, do not treat the already-resolved closePromise as a new proof, and do not add finite responsibility expiry.
findings.actual_branch_counterfactual: Drive actual main with close already observed but proc unknown, then restored known-same epoch, then gone; it must not return or write final before the required terminal proof. Separately cover close-before-cleanup and no-birth error+close/no-exit using actual runner rather than cleanupChild alone.

findings.title: Actual runner's no-child asynchronous failure dereferences a null epoch
findings.trigger: spawn returns a ChildProcess with pid undefined and later emits EAGAIN/ENOENT plus close and no exit. runPilot makes epoch=null then reads epoch.presence synchronously, before the normal async error can arrive.
findings.impact: The primary becomes a TypeError instead of the real startup failure; cleanup initially returns unknown because errorSeen has not yet fired. main later uses its generic held path instead of the otherwise implemented no-child-confirmed route. The ledger does retain the later error/close, so this defect alone is not claimed to orphan a never-born child.
findings.contract: R4 SPEC actual no-child async error+close/no-exit route, original failure preservation and correct tagged no-child outcome.
findings.minimal_fix: Handle no PID without dereferencing null; wait for the actual error/close facts through the owned ledger, then finish no-child-confirmed with original startup error. Keep born/unknown distinct and preserve NF-01 safeguards.
findings.actual_branch_counterfactual: Exercise actual runPilot/main with pid undefined and error+close scheduled next tick. Assert original EAGAIN/ENOENT, no-child-confirmed and no TypeError; not only the current cleanupChild helper test with events pre-emitted.

findings.title: Fresh identity verification omits its PPID comparison
findings.trigger: A mocked fresh identity has the correct PID/startticks/group/session but a different PPID; hello.ppid still equals toolPid. verifyCustodianIdentity accepts it because only hello.ppid, not fresh.identity.ppid, is checked against the tool.
findings.impact: The strict identity assertion is weaker than reported. For this exact fixed nofork ChildProcess with the tool alive, the direct-child relationship already strongly constrains real PPID; I do not invent a current foreign-parent signalling exploit. The later live-child signal check does compare fresh PPID against its recorded epoch.
findings.contract: Exact task requires genuine fresh full C epoch including PPID, not only the HELLO claim.
findings.minimal_fix: Compare fresh.identity.ppid to toolPid and the recorded spawned child epoch; add the missing wrong-fresh-PPID counterfactual in the new test only.
findings.actual_branch_counterfactual: Actual verifier with wrong fresh PPID must refuse even when HELLO claims the correct parent.

findings.title: Four captured failed runs are mislabeled as five
findings.trigger: Report says five failed captures, but raw result/exit/log records test001..004 are exit1 and test005 is exit0/38 of38; both syntax checks are exit0.
findings.impact: A count error in the report, not a fabricated code safety blocker. Historical failures remain valid retained evidence and earlier UNRECORDED trials remain unreconstructable.
findings.contract: Actual capture metadata/raw logs determine history; success must not be counted as failure or erase earlier failures.
findings.minimal_fix: Append an evidence correction to the author's own new report when separately authorized; do not overwrite captures. This reviewer leaves all old reports/evidence unchanged.
findings.actual_branch_counterfactual: No runtime needed: compare the seven recorded result/exit/log SHA256 triples and TAP totals.
findings.runtime: NOT_RUN by reviewer; existing artifacts read and hashed
